full_judgment: 3. Respondent Nos. 2 and 5—The Chairman, Land Reform Board and the Chief Manager of Court of Wards—respectively have entered appearances and have filed affidavit-in-opposition. These respondents upon denying the correctness of the material averments made in the writ petition have stated, inter alia, that the title i.e. Nowab, is not an inheritable one and that the claim of the petitioners as of being Nawab is unfounded and unsustainable one; that the claim of the petitioners that they and respondents Nos. 6-8, 10-34, 36-39 and 41-47, hereinafter referred to as said respondents, are the present sole exclusive heirs/successors is not correct, that neither the petitioners nor the said respondents had established their claim of inheritance and succession by any cogent evidence before the Court of Wards; that the petitioners nor the said respondents have filed any papers showing that they are the sole proprietor of the property which was placed under the management of the Court of Wards; that almost 50% of the wards of the original owner had left Bangladesh and that their whereabouts were not known, as such, their property has assumed the character of abandoned property and that vested in the Government as per provision of President's Order No.16 of 1972; that the said respondents have not filed any paper before the Court of Wards in support of their claim of being proprietor of the property managed by the Court of Wards, nor they have approached the Court of Wards seeking release of the property from the management thereof, that joint proprietorship has not been partitioned and, as such, the Court of Wards in the absence of determination of share of the petitioners as well as the said respondents and other proprietors of the property, in law, cannot release the property to the petitioners and the said respondents, that the petitioners have not made any statement as to how the mortgaged properties were redeemed and discharged from the mortgage debt, nor the petitioners have given any particulars and description of the property which was the subject matter of the mortgage; that it is not correct that the Court of Wards did not furnish any statement of account of repayment of debt either to the Nowab Khaja Salimullah Bahadur or to any of his heirs or successors, or it is correct that the petitioners and the said respondents were ignored about the matter; that the petitioners' contention of repayment of loan out of income of the mortgaged property and that even after repayment and disbursement of amount for which the property was mortgaged the Court of Wards was retaining the possession of the mortgaged property illegally is not correct; that it is not correct that before and after acquisition of rent receiving interest the officers of the Court of Wards in collusion with designing persons leased out, sold and otherwise disposed of various moveable and immovable mortgaged properties and mis-appropriated wholly or partly the proceeds of the mortgage property, that as there is ample provision under the Court of Wards Act for adjudication of the dispute of the kind as stated in the writ petition and that the petitioners having had not resorted to that forum the writ petition so filed is not maintainable; that it has not been established by any competent Court that the petitioners as well as the said respondents are the heirs and successors of Nowab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah Bahadur and that they are the proprietors of the estate jointly or individually; that the matter of succession to the property of the estate by the petitioners and the said respondent being a disputed question and, as such, the Court of Wards cannot release the property until the dispute is resolved or determined by a competent Civil Court, that the petitioners ought to have reported to the Court of Wards for settlement of their claim in respect of the property in the light of the provision of the Court of Wards Act; that as there is conflicting claim amongst the wards and that joint proprietorship as has not been partitioned, the Court of Wards cannot release the property in favour of the petitioners and the said respondents.
